'''Lucia Beatriz Rothman-Denes''' (born February 17, 1943) is an Argentinian American microbiologist who is the A. J. Carlson Professor in the Department of [[Molecular genetics|Molecular Genetics]] at the [[University of Chicago]]. She is known for studying the regulation of [[Transcription (biology)|transcription]] and [[Host (biology)|host]] interactions that occur during bacterial virus infection. She was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS) in 2014.

== Early life and education ==
Rothman-Denes was born in [[Buenos Aires]] in 1943 to Boris and Carmen Rothman.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/lucia-b-rothman-denes-gioemy/|title=Lucia Rothman-Denes|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref> She studied at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] and graduated in 1964 with a [[Licentiate (degree)|licenciada]] degree in [[chemistry]].<ref name=":0" /> She remained there for her graduate studies, earning a PhD in [[biochemistry]] in 1967.<ref name=":1"/> She worked at the [[Leloir Institute]]. Rothman-Denes completed a [[postdoctoral]] [[fellow]]ship at the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name=":0" /> She also spent time at the [[University of California, San Diego]] with [[E. Peter Geiduschek]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://library.ucsd.edu/speccoll/findingaids/mss0737.html|title=Register of E. Peter Geiduschek Laboratory Records - MSS 0737|website=library.ucsd.edu|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1967, Rothman-Denes was appointed to the faculty at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://micro.uchicago.edu/program/faculty/lucia-rothman-denes|title=Lucia Rothman-Denes {{!}} Microbiology|website=micro.uchicago.edu|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref> She was made a Full Professor in 1984, and the A. J. Carlson Professor in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sciencelife.uchospitals.edu/2014/05/01/lucia-rothman-denes-professor-of-molecular-genetics-and-cell-biology-elected-to-national-academy-of-sciences/|title=Lucia Rothman-Denes. Professor of Molecular Genetics and Cell Biology, Elected to National Academy of Sciences|last=Jiang|first=Kevin|date=2014-05-01|website=Science Life|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sciencelife.uchospitals.edu/2015/01/28/three-ucm-faculty-receive-named-professorships/|title=Three UCM faculty receive named professorships|last=Jiang|first=Kevin|date=2015-01-28|website=Science Life|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref> She studies how bacterial viruses impact the molecular processes within a host.<ref name=":0" /> She uncovered mechanisms of transcription regulation through [[DNA]] structural transitions. Rothman-Denes combines biophysical, biochemical and structural characterisation techniques to understand gene expression at the level of transcription.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/lucia-b-rothman-denes|title=Lucia B. Rothman-Denes|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref> She is particularly interested in DNA-dependent [[RNA polymerase]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://mgcb.uchicago.edu/faculty/rothman-denes/|title=MGCB / Faculty - Rothman-Denes Group|website=mgcb.uchicago.edu|access-date=2019-05-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325111637/http://mgcb.uchicago.edu/faculty/rothman-denes/|archive-date=2018-03-25|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Rothman-Denes' current work considers the mechanism at the onset of an injection, when proteins and genomes are injected into a host.<ref name=":1" /> She is also working on the characterisation of viral-encoded products that inhibit the essential function of the host. She studies the target of these viral-encoded products in an effort to design new [[antibiotic]]s.<ref name=":0" /> She served on the board of governors of the [[American Society for Microbiology]] from 2000 to 2003.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

* 2001 Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uchicago.edu/about/accolades/13/|title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|last=AvenueChicago|first=The University of ChicagoEdward H. Levi Hall5801 South Ellis|last2=Us|first2=Illinois 60637773 702 1234 Contact|website=The University of Chicago|language=en|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref>
* 2014 Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uchicagomedicine.org/forefront/news/2014/may/lucia-rothmandenes-professor-of-molecular-genetics-and-cell-biology-elected-to-national-academy-of-s|title=Lucia RothmanDenes Professor of Molecular Genetics and Cell Biology elected to National Academy of S - UChicago Medicine|website=www.uchicagomedicine.org|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref>

Rothman-Denes holds several patents to protect her inventions, including novel [[RNA polymerase]]s and transcription substrates.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/lucia-b-rothman-denes|title=Lucia B. Rothman-Denes Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com|access-date=2019-05-09}}</ref>
